title: Add minimal “hello inference” snippet + improve first-run errors
author: Jada Williams
release_notes:
- TS SDK: add copy/paste “hello inference” snippet and runnable example
- Improve first-run errors for missing API key / common misconfigurations (actionable message + link to docs)
- Minor README restructuring to surface Quickstart + streaming pointer
body:
## Context
We’re seeing a non-trivial dropoff for TS users between “install SDK” and “first successful request”. Two recurring issues from Support + Growth: (1) users don’t have a minimal snippet they can copy/paste without context switching, and (2) the first error they hit (missing key / bad env var / wrong base URL) is terse and not obviously actionable.

This PR adds a minimal “hello inference” snippet to the README and a runnable example under `examples/` that mirrors the activation milestone (first 2xx completion). It also improves first-run error messages to reduce time-to-first-success.

## What’s included
- README: add a minimal snippet (single file, no framework) that uses `REDWOOD_API_KEY` and prints the first completion.
- Examples: add `examples/hello-inference.ts` + `pnpm example:hello` script.
- Errors: make missing/empty API key errors explicit and include a direct link to the docs + Console page where users create keys.
- Errors: improve messaging for common mistakes:
  - `REDWOOD_API_KEY` present but whitespace/placeholder
  - accidentally using `OPENAI_API_KEY`
  - passing a base URL without protocol
  - 401/403: add suggestion to verify key scope + project selection

## Why this approach
- Keeps the “happy path” to <60 seconds: `pnpm add`, set env var, run snippet.
- “Actionable errors” > “generic errors”: we keep the underlying error type but add a short hint and next step.

## Manual test plan
1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
2. Run example with no env var -> expect explicit missing key message.
3. Run with `REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...` -> expect successful response.
4. Run with placeholder key -> expect validation error that points to docs.
5. Run with invalid key -> expect 401/403 hint + request id surfaced.

## Notes
- No API surface changes (non-breaking). Only refines error strings and adds docs/examples.
- This is intentionally minimal and aligned with lifecycle activation work (first success). We can iterate later to add a streaming example once the baseline snippet is performing well.
commits: docs(readme): add “hello inference” quick snippet and restructure quickstart section
feat(examples): add hello-inference runnable script + package.json entry
feat(errors): improve missing/invalid API key messages and common misconfig hints
chore(ci): run lint/format on touched files
changed_areas: src/client.ts (first-run env var validation + error hints)
src/errors.ts (richer messages for auth + config errors)
review_conversation:
Ben Carter (Growth): Can we make sure the missing-key error points to the *exact* console path we’re using in onboarding emails? Also please avoid any claim-y language in README (“fastest” etc.).

Jada Williams (author): Yep — updated the link to `/console/api-keys` (same as email CTA) and kept copy neutral. Also added a short “Troubleshooting” anchor so emails can deep-link.

Soojin Lee (PMM): +1 on neutral copy. For the 401/403 hint, can we avoid implying the platform is down? Maybe suggest verifying project + key scope first, then retry.

Jada Williams (author): Done. Adjusted wording to “Verify API key + project scope” and included request id in the message to help Support.

Nikhil Sharma (PM): Looks good. One ask: if users accidentally set `OPENAI_API_KEY`, can we detect and hint? It’s very common.

Jada Williams (author): Added a lightweight check: if `REDWOOD_API_KEY` is missing but `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set, we include a one-line hint in the error.

Ben Carter (Growth): Approved after last push. This should help activation time.

Status: Approved (2), merged via squash.
